name: Gerber StrongArm Fixed Blade Knife
summary: A full-tang outdoor utility knife for camp repairs and controlled cutting tasks. The selected reference pairs a black plain-edge blade with a coyote brown grip and sheath; match the selected Canadian offer before buying.
description: A fixed blade makes sense when a camp task calls for a secure grip and a tool that is ready without unfolding. The StrongArm reference documented here is Gerber’s coyote brown plain-edge version. Its coated blade and textured grip suit comparison for cordage, campsite repairs and routine field maintenance. Carry weight, sheath retention and maintenance matter as much as the headline dimensions. The recorded Canadian link does not authenticate a delivered knife or current seller.

pros: Fixed-blade construction avoids a folding pivot for routine outdoor utility work.
Textured grip and several documented sheath mounting options support pack planning.
cons: A fixed blade occupies more pack space than a small folding utility tool.
Check actual sheath retention and mounting hardware; illustration proportions are conceptual.

useCases: Compare a dedicated camp cutting tool for cordage and equipment repairs.
Plan secure storage and maintenance alongside gloves, lighting and a separate repair tool.

safetyNotes: Use only for lawful outdoor utility tasks. Check applicable Canadian laws, local rules and venue restrictions before transport or carrying; self-defence carry is not automatically lawful.
Keep the edge and point away from the body and other people. Use a stable work area and store the knife securely in a properly retaining sheath, out of reach of children.
Inspect the blade, handle and sheath before use. Do not use a damaged tool or treat it as an electrical tool, pry bar or substitute for an appropriate saw.
Follow the delivered manufacturer instructions for cleaning, sharpening and storage. This profile is documentary research, not a physical test or authentication of an individual knife.
